page.backCopy: The source supplies context. The project evidence remains in the files, prototypes, and results elsewhere in the lab.

books.title: A New Solution to the Random Assignment Problem
books.citation: Anna Bogomolnaia and Hervé Moulin · Journal of Economic Theory 100(2)
books.summary: Introduces Probabilistic Serial as a random-assignment mechanism and makes its trade-offs explicit: ordinal efficiency and envy-freeness improve, while strategy-proofness does not survive.
books.excerpt: PS is envy-free, RP is not; RP is strategy-proof, PS is not.
books.annotation: This reference informed the project’s simultaneous-eating stage and clarified the mechanism-level tradeoffs behind probabilistic assignment.
books.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

books.title: A Solution to the Random Assignment Problem on the Full Preference Domain
books.citation: Akshay-Kumar Katta and Jay Sethuraman · Journal of Economic Theory 131(1)
books.summary: Extends random assignment beyond strict rankings by allowing indifference between objects, reinterpreting Probabilistic Serial as an iterative network-flow problem.
books.excerpt: Agents are allowed to be indifferent between objects.
books.annotation: This reference extends the project’s theoretical foundation beyond strict preference rankings by considering cases in which participants may be indifferent between options.
books.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

books.title: Three Observations on Linear Algebra
books.citation: Garrett Birkhoff · Universidad Nacional de Tucumán, Revista A 5
books.summary: The decomposition result behind converting a fractional allocation matrix into a weighted collection of deterministic assignments.
books.excerpt: A probability matrix can describe many possible concrete allocations, not just one final outcome.
books.annotation: In the project, decomposition is the bridge between an abstract fractional result and a lottery over assignments that can actually be issued to students.
books.provenance: USED IN THE ORIGINAL COURSE-ALLOCATION PRESENTATION

books.title: How Should We Normalize Electromyograms?
books.citation: Adrian Burden · Journal of Electromyography and Kinesiology 20(6)
books.summary: Reviews EMG normalization methods and supports maximal voluntary contraction as a useful reference while warning that normalization does not automatically reveal absolute muscle capacity.
books.excerpt: Neither method is guaranteed to reveal maximal activation capacity.
books.annotation: This supports careful language for the EMG device: relative activation inferred from an individual reference, not a direct measurement of mechanical force.
books.provenance: BACKGROUND READING / NOT CLAIMED AS AN ORIGINAL PROJECT SOURCE

books.title: Integrating Health in Urban and Territorial Planning
books.citation: World Health Organization and UN-Habitat · Sourcebook
books.summary: Connects planning decisions with transport, housing, food, education, healthcare, environment, well-being, and health equity rather than reducing urban quality of life to one indicator.
books.excerpt: The way we plan and build our cities defines our quality of life.
books.annotation: The Shanghai project followed a smaller, local version of this logic: ask residents what matters, then translate nearby services and walking time into something visible.
books.provenance: BACKGROUND READING / NOT CLAIMED AS AN ORIGINAL PROJECT SOURCE

books.title: EMGFilters Implementation Reference
books.summary: A reusable sample-by-sample filtering component for EMG streams, with configurable anti-hum, low-pass, and high-pass stages.
books.excerpt: Integrated as a reference component; not presented as original filter design.
books.annotation: The filter is an integrated dependency, not an algorithm authored from scratch for this project. The project work begins with calibration, Kalman filtering, band assignment, and session aggregation.
